title: Priority-based scheduler and hierarchical burst-credit ledger for Dedicated fleets
author: Aisha Patel
commit_messages: implement priority scheduler loop with tenant queue priorities and weight buckets
add hierarchical burst credit ledger, decay worker, and persistence migration
expose /v1/dedicated/credits API and metrics for telemetry; add unit + e2e tests
docs: describe new config fields and migration steps; add console view for credits
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets require predictable throughput guarantees while supporting short, high-priority bursts. Existing shared-burst/token-pool approaches lack per-tenant hierarchies and do not support explicit priority preemption between workloads. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a priority-aware scheduler for Dedicated serving nodes that implements weighted priority queues, inter-tenant fairness windows, and optional preemption for critical requests; and 2) a hierarchical burst-credit ledger that allocates, debits, and decays burst credits at both tenant and sub-tenant (team/route) levels so operators can define parent/child quotas and emergency reserve pools. Design summary: The scheduler maintains per-tenant queues with three priority tiers (critical, high, default) and weight buckets inside each tier. Requests are scored by (priority, age, weight) so urgent requests jump ahead only when credits permit; a pluggable preemption hook can evict low-priority queued executions when a critical request times out waiting. The ledger issues credits on a configurable cadence, supports token transfers between children and parents, and records a decay timeline to avoid permanent credit hoarding. Credits are persisted in the existing KV store with a lightweight migration that adds ledger entries under the dedicated/credits namespace. API and telemetry: Adds /v1/dedicated/credits endpoints to query balances, transfer credits, and inspect decay history. New metrics: dedicated.burst_credit_balance, dedicated.burst_credit_allocated, dedicated.preempt_count, scheduler.queue_depth_by_priority, scheduler.weighted_fair_utilization. Console: new CreditsOverview panel showing per-tenant balances, recent transfers, and predicted refill times. Config changes and migration: Adds new fields to dedicated_autoscaler.yaml: priority_scheduling.enabled (bool), ledger.hierarchy.enabled (bool), ledger.decay.window_seconds (int), ledger.default_refill_rate (tokens/sec), scheduler.preemption.enabled (bool), scheduler.max_preempt_percent (0-100). Migration path is provided in redwood/docs/ops/dedicated-migration.md and the migration_202603.go makes the ledger durable and backfills a conservative starting balance for existing tenants. Tests and CI: Unit tests cover scheduler scoring, edge cases around priority inversion, and race conditions; integration tests simulate hierarchical transfers and decay; perf sims approximate mixed workloads to validate impact on p99 latency. Initial CI run failed due to a data race in the ledger's in-memory cache; fixed by adding a mutex and a test that stresses concurrent transfers. Deployment plan and rollout: Feature behind dedicated.priority_scheduler feature flag; default OFF for existing clusters. Plan: 1) merge to main with migration but flag off, 2) deploy migration job during a maintenance window (recommended), 3) canary-enable for a small dedicated fleet, monitor dedicated.burst_credit_balance and preempt_count for anomalies, 4) progressively enable for more fleets and flip default to ON in a follow-up PR. Backwards compatibility: API adds endpoints and config keys but keeps previous token-pool behavior as a compatibility mode when ledger.hierarchy.enabled=false. Observability and alerts: Added alert if preempt_count spikes above configured threshold or if total allocated credits exceed safety cap for a fleet. Rollback: feature flag off reverts runtime behavior; migration is additive but includes a reversible backfill marker; instructions included in ops docs. Related: builds on ENG-4120 autoscaler telemetry work and complements SRE-241's per-fleet SLA tooling. See linked Linear tickets for perf targets and follow-ups.
review_comments: Tomás Rivera: Overall design looks sound; two high-level asks: add formal proof/argument for starvation avoidance in the README, and ensure migration is reversible for at least 7 days. Also please benchmark p99 impact with mixed-tenant workloads.

Aisha Patel (author): Added an analysis section to redwood/serving/scheduler/README.md describing the fairness invariant and provided time-to-live markers for migration backfill so operators can revert allocations by deleting the backfill tag within 7 days.

Lena Cho: Found a race in ledger.go under concurrent transfer; CI caught it. After the mutex fix the integration tests look stable. Please add a unit that simulates N concurrent transfers to the same parent key.
Aisha Patel: Added stress test in dedicated_credit_ledger_test.go that runs 200 concurrent transfers and validates invariants; pushing updated commit.

Marcus Hall (SRE): Approve with comment: recommend an observability dashboard tile for total reserved vs used credits so on-call can quickly see if someone is draining a shared reserve. We added a dashboard yml and alerted on safety cap breach.
CI Bot: initial pipeline failed on race detector; subsequent run passed. Full e2e pipeline passed on second run.
release_notes: Add priority scheduler and hierarchical burst-credit ledger for Dedicated fleets. New config flags: dedicated.priority_scheduling, ledger.hierarchy, scheduler.preemption. Migration job included; feature gated by feature flag. New metrics and console panel for credit visibility. See docs/ops/dedicated-migration.md for upgrade steps.
